question: What is the atomic mass of oxygen?
solution:
The correct answer is __**16 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atomic Mass:** The atomic mass of an element is defined as the mass of its atom expressed in atomic mass units (**u**). For oxygen, the atomic mass is **16 u**.
 
• **Oxygen's Isotope:** The most abundant isotope of oxygen is **Oxygen-16**, which has 8 protons and 8 neutrons, resulting in an atomic mass of **16 u**.
 
• **Periodic Table:** Oxygen is represented by the symbol **O** in the periodic table and is located in Group 16 (Chalcogens) and Period 2.
 
• **Significance:** The atomic mass is crucial for chemical calculations, including determining the molar mass of compounds that include oxygen.
 
• **Incorrect Options:** **18 u** refers to the molecular mass of water (H₂O), **8 u** is incorrect as it only accounts for protons, and **12 u** corresponds to the atomic mass of carbon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isotopes of Oxygen:** Oxygen exists in three isotopes: **Oxygen-16**, **Oxygen-17**, and **Oxygen-18**. Among these, **Oxygen-16** is the most abundant, comprising over **99.76%** of naturally occurring oxygen.
 
• **Properties:** Oxygen is a highly reactive non-metal and is essential for life. It is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust and atmosphere.
 
• **Applications:** Oxygen is widely used in industries such as **steel production**, **medical oxygen therapy**, and **water treatment**. It is also vital for combustion processes.
 
• **Molecular Oxygen:** Oxygen commonly exists as a diatomic molecule (**O₂**) in nature. The molecular mass of oxygen gas is **32 u** (16 u × 2).
 
• **Discovery:** Oxygen was discovered by **Carl Wilhelm Scheele** in 1772 and independently by **Joseph Priestley** in 1774. The name "oxygen" was coined by **Antoine Lavoisier**, who demonstrated its role in combustion and respiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (u):** An atomic mass unit is defined as one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom. It is approximately **1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg**.
 
• **Periodic Table Context:** Oxygen is the eighth element in the periodic table, with an atomic number of **8**, representing its number of protons.
 
• **Role in Compounds:** Oxygen forms numerous compounds, including oxides, acids, and organic molecules. It is part of water (H₂O), which is essential for all forms of life.
 
• **Reactivity:** Oxygen readily forms bonds with other elements due to its high electronegativity (**3.44** on the Pauling scale).
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Oxygen is critical for maintaining life on Earth and is involved in processes such as **photosynthesis** and **respiration**. However, excessive oxygen in water bodies can lead to issues like **eutrophication**.
